text:
sam: kicking off 2.8.0 canary to 10% in us-west / eu-west now. keeping an eye on p95 and error budget :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started for release v2.8.0 -> 10% traffic. monitoring: p95_latency, error_rate, kvcache_miss_rate
maya: seeing a p95 bump in eu-west already, ~30% above baseline. noticed increased kvcache miss rate on a few backends
leo: can you paste the query that repros? maya: nothing deterministic yet, just telemetry spikes from several customers hitting long contexts. logs show `kvcache.miss_rate: 0.34` and `kernel_fwd_time: +120ms`
sam: if kvcache miss is causal we might avoid rollback by forcing a warm prefix cache, but that's risky mid-rollout
anne: deploy-bot shows autorevert disabled for this rollout (manual strategy). we need consensus for manual rollback or continue monitoring
paul: quick comms note — if we rollback we should pin dedicated pools to v2.7.9 and publish a short release note explaining perf regression + mitigation ETA
leo: ops question — do we have an immediate mitigation? maybe reduce batch size or limit seq_len to 1024 for canary traffic?
maya: reducing max_seq_len in-flight helped reduce kernel time in staging last week. could push a temporary routing rule to cap seq_len for canary traffic
sam: option matrix: A) manual rollback to 2.7.9 now, pin dedicated pools, send customer note; B) apply temporary seq_len cap and observe for 10m; C) keep canary running and escalate to research. what's the room?
anne: prefer B short test (10m) + go to A if p95 stays >20% over baseline. agree on comm wording now so we can send quickly if we rollback
paul: drafting two short blurbs: one for internal release notes and one customer-facing. internal: "Rollback to v2.7.9 due to increased p95 latency observed in canary, mitigation: pin and investigate kvcache eviction behavior". customer: "We've paused rollout of a performance update and reverted to the previous version while we investigate latency for long-context requests."
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary throttle applied: seq_len_max=1024 for v2.8.0 traffic slice eu-west. will re-evaluate in 10m.
maya: thanks — telemetry already trending down in eu-west after cap, p95 back to ~+8% over baseline at 3m
leo: good sign. still keep error budget watch, but i'm leaning to keep canary rolling after 10m if stable
sam: agreed. anne, can you prep rollback playbook and ops pin steps in case we revert? include sample `kubectl` pin commands and the release-note blurb from paul
anne: on it. cc @paul — I'll paste the pin command and the customer blurb into the rollback checklist now
paul: ack — will finalize the customer note and post to #announcements if we revert. also tagging legal for minor blurb signoff (emoji :white_check_mark:)
deploy-bot: deploybot: monitoring update: eu-west p95 latency at +9% over baseline after 8m. no spike in error_rate. autorevert still disabled
sam: we'll wait until 10m mark and reconvene. if p95 >20% or errors spike we rollback. otherwise continue rollout but keep seq_len cap for another hour and follow up with research postmortem
paul: drafting message for customers in case we roll back — will post to #customer-communications draft channel for review
leo: thx all. please react with :thumbsup: when you approve the contingency plan (B then A threshold).
maya: :thumbsup:
anne: :thumbsup:
paul: :thumbsup:
sam: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploybot: 10m canary check complete — condition met to continue with restricted rollout (seq_len cap). no rollback executed.
paul: publishing internal note to release docs and marking rollback playbook as "ready" for immediate execution if needed later.
